extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory; specialists in inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of criteria, hypotheses, and interpretive remarks used in proving Diophantine inequalities (Corollary 2.3) for hyperbolic curves in the context of inter-universal Teichmüller theory. Focuses on required hypotheses, reductions, notational conventions, and methodological ingredients invoked in the proofs and comparisons with prior work (e.g., Faltings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diophantine inequality (Corollary 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over a number field, D a reduced divisor, UX = X \ D a hyperbolic curve, d ∈ Z_{>0}, ε ∈ R_{>0}, write ω_X for the canonical sheaf. Then one has an inequality of 'bounded discrepancy classes' on UX(Q)^{≤d}: ht_{ω_X(D)} ≺_{BD} (1+ε)(log-diﬀ_X + log-cond_D) (i.e., (1+ε)(log-diﬀ_X + log-cond_D) − ht_{ω_X(D)} is bounded below on UX(Q)^{≤d}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corollary is presented as equivalent to [GenEll], Theorem 2.1 (i); the proof reduces to verifying [GenEll], Theorem 2.1 (ii) under explicit reductions (see reduction-to-P^1 item). The inequality is an assertion of bounded discrepancy classes (BD-classes) and the text references definitions and remarks in [GenEll] for the precise meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbolicity criterion for UX
rubrics_metrics.description: UX is a hyperbolic curve precisely when deg(ω_X(D)) > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the hypothesis used to ensure the diophantine inequality applies; it appears explicitly in the statement of Corollary 2.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to P^1 with D = {0,1,∞} and KV hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove Corollary 2.3 it suffices (without loss of generality) to assume Q = P^1, X = P^1, D = {0,1,∞}, and that KV ⊆ UX(Q) is a compactly bounded subset whose support contains the nonarchimedean prime 2 and which satisfies the condition '(∗j-inv)' of Corollary 2.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof proceeds by reduction to this explicit model case; the text notes that the '(∗j-inv)' condition concerns the behaviour of KV as UX(Q)^{≤d} varies and is vacuous in fixed-d situations. The support-containing-2 and (∗j-inv) conditions are explicit hypotheses needed to apply earlier corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / convention for 'compactly bounded subset' KV ⊆ U(Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'compactly bounded subset' KV ⊆ U(Q) ⊆ X(Q) is a subset which is compactly bounded as a subset of X(Q) and furthermore satisfies: for each v in the archimedean set V^{arc} (resp. v in V^{non}), the compact domain K_v ⊆ X^{arc} (resp. K_v ⊆ X(Q_v)) is contained in U(C) ⊆ X(C) (resp. U(Q_v) ⊆ X(Q_v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention is to be applied in the statements of [GenEll], Theorem 2.1; Lemma 3.7; Theorem 3.8; Corollary 4.4, and in the present paper's uses of 'compactly bounded subset'. The remark emphasizes that although not explicit in [GenEll], this is implicit in its Introduction and in proofs involving compactly bounded subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notational convention for BD-class inequalities (α ≺_F β)
rubrics_metrics.description: In [GenEll], Definition 1.2 (ii) the notation 'α ≺_F β' corresponds to 'α(x) − β(x) ≤ C'; the opposite direction 'α ≻_F β' corresponds to 'β(x) − α(x) ≤ C'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This correction is explicitly stated in Remark 2.3.1 (ii); adopt this ordering when interpreting displays and BD-class inequalities in the paper and referenced results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharpness of the constant '1' in Corollary 2.3
rubrics_metrics.description: The constant '1' appearing in the inequality of Corollary 2.3 cannot be improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This non-improvability is justified by examples constructed in [Mss] and relates to failures of the theory when one replaces the first power of the étale theta function by its N-th power (N ≥ 2). The remark connects this sharpness to invariance properties of global height under certain isogenies and to arguments in [IUTchIII] and [GenEll], Lemma 3.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: log-volumes of log-shells measure distortion of integral structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-volumes of log-shells may be regarded as numerical measures of distortions of the integral structure (relative to the 'arithmetic holomorphic' integral structures determined by local rings of integers 'O') that arise from the log-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretive description explains the origin of certain terms in the inequalities and motivates the application of analytic number theory (prime number theorem) to sum such local contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Prime Number Theorem in the analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The term '* · l' in Theorem 1.10 computations arises by applying the prime number theorem (Proposition 1.6) to sum log-volumes of log-shells at various nonarchimedean primes of the number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that estimates from the prime number theorem are closely related to aspects of the Riemann zeta function discussed elsewhere; this method treats primes 'one by one' as opposed to global-density approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of auxiliary prime l (condition C1 / heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: In computations (notably Corollary 2.2 (ii) and condition (C1)) the auxiliary prime l is taken to be roughly of the order of the square root of the height of the elliptic curve under consideration; l is thus a rough numerical proxy for the moduli of the elliptic curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guides the scale at which l should be chosen in the arguments — the heuristic links height, moduli, and the analytic terms appearing in the inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain of modular Frobenius liftings
rubrics_metrics.description: Modular Frobenius liftings of [pOrd] are not defined over the (algebraic) moduli stack of hyperbolic curves over Z_p but over a p-adic formal algebraic stack (formally étale over the algebraic moduli stack) given by the canonical lifting to Z_p of the moduli stack of hyperbolic curves equipped with a nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies where certain Frobenius-lifting objects live and is used to explain gaps between 'p-adically analytic' and algebraic moduli stacks; it motivates analytic continuation constructions (Belyi maps, open immersions) invoked in later arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: non-perfect schemes reflected by Frobenius failure
rubrics_metrics.description: The gap between perfect and non-perfect schemes in positive characteristic is precisely reflected in the extent to which the Frobenius morphism on the scheme fails to be an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used conceptually to relate issues in positive characteristic geometry (and p-adic Teichmüller theory) to arithmetic distortions measured in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of 'essential ingredients' in Faltings' approach (summary items a–g)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rough list of essential ingredients in the case of [Falt]: (a) elementary algebraic number theory related to the geometry of numbers (heights, Hermite–Minkowski), (b) global class field theory, (c) p-adic Hodge–Tate theory, (d) p-adic theory of finite flat group schemes, (e) generalities about isogenies and Tate modules of abelian varieties, (f) polarizations of abelian varieties, (g) logarithmic geometry of toroidal compactifications of the moduli stack of abelian varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are presented to compare the 'essential ingredients' of Faltings' methods with the ingredients used in IUT; each item is then mapped to analogous or contrasting roles in the inter-universal theory throughout the subsequent discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition of global class field theory into primitive components (b-1–b-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A technical dissection of global class field theory used in [Lang1]: (b-1) local class field theory of p-adic local fields; (b-2) theory of global density of primes; (b-3) elementary algebraic number theory results giving the Unit Theorem; (b-4) the global reciprocity law (existence of a conductor for the Artin symbol); (b-5) Kummer theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses this decomposition to compare the roles of these components in classical approaches with how analogous phenomena are handled in IUT (e.g., via Prime Number Theorem techniques, Kummer-theoretic constructions, or cyclotomic rigidity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological contrast: global reciprocity maps vs Kummer-theoretic isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Kummer-theoretic isomorphisms satisfy very strong covariant functoriality properties, whereas reciprocity maps in class field theory tend not to satisfy such functoriality (they are often contravariant with respect to functions and require duality to reverse direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrast motivates the central role of Kummer theory in IUT (due to its 'general nonsense' functoriality) and explains why class field-theoretic reciprocity maps are less suitable for the evaluation-of-functions techniques needed in IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical/methodological stance: Prime Number Theorem vs global density
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach using the Prime Number Theorem treats primes 'one by one' (deactivating aggregations of primes) whereas the classical global-density perspective aggregates primes coherently; this difference mirrors the dismantling of arithmetic-holomorphic structures in IUT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This viewpoint is used to justify analytic number theory methods in the paper and to explain conceptual differences between IUT and classical scheme-theoretic methods like those used in Faltings' proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of local class field theory for multiradial cyclotomic rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Local class field theory can be applied in IUT only 'of limited use' to obtain cyclotomic rigidity algorithms for MLF-Galois pairs; the resulting algorithms are uniradial (fail to be multiradial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation supports the necessity of more elaborate (multiradial) cyclotomic rigidity algorithms in the development of IUT, and explains why simple local-class-field-theory inputs are insufficient for full multiradial structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive correspondence: 'canonical number' ↔ modular Frobenius liftings
rubrics_metrics.description: A conceptual correspondence asserted in the text: 'canonical number' corresponds to modular Frobenius liftings (in the analogy with p-adic Teichmüller theory and the notions discussed earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a guiding interpretive principle used to link arithmetic-numerical objects ('canonical numbers') with geometric/Galois-theoretic constructions (modular Frobenius liftings) throughout the paper's arguments.
